### B.1 Spike-and-slab Gibbs update rules for linear model

Suppose we have the following hierarchical model,

$$ \displaystyle y_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(x_{i}\beta,\sigma^{2}), \displaystyle\beta_{j}\sim(1-\pi)\delta_{0}+\pi\mathcal{N}(\mu,\tau^{2}), \displaystyle\pi_{j}\sim\text{ Bern }(\theta), \displaystyle\sigma^{2}\sim\text{ InvGamma }(a_{1},a_{2}), \displaystyle\tau^{2}\sim\text{ InvGamma }(b_{1},b_{2}), \displaystyle\theta\sim\text{ Beta }(A,B), \displaystyle\mu\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{0},\tau_{0}^{2}). $$

Each iteration consists of regression update and hyper-parameters update.

- • Update $\pi_{j}$ In regression update step, we update each feature $j$ randomly and once at a time, so it’s essentially the same as in the 1d regression problem. $\displaystyle\frac{P(\pi_{j}=0\mid\cdot)}{P(\pi_{j}=1\mid\cdot)}$ $\displaystyle=\frac{p_{0}}{1-p_{0}}\times\frac{P(y\mid X,\pi_{j}=0)}{P(y\mid X,\pi_{j}=1)}$ (B.1) $\displaystyle=\frac{p_{0}}{1-p_{0}}\times\text{det}(Q)^{1/2}\exp(-\frac{\tau^{2}}{2\sigma^{4}}(y-\mu)^{T}XQX^{T}(y-\mu))$ (B.2) $\displaystyle\quad\times\exp(-\frac{1}{2\sigma^{2}}||y||^{2}+\frac{1}{2\sigma^{2}}||y-\mu||^{2}),$ (B.3) where $Q=Q_{j}=1+\frac{\tau^{2}}{\sigma^{2}}||x_{j}||^{2}$ is a scalar and we denote the residual $r_{i}:=y_{i}-\sum_{l\neq j}x_{il}\beta_{l}$ , which satisfies

$$ r_{i}:=y_{i}-\sum_{l\neq j}x_{il}\beta_{l}=x_{ij}\beta_{j}+\epsilon_{i}. $$

- • Update $\beta_{j}$ When the other features except $j$ are fixed, consider the model $r_{i}=x_{ij}\beta_{j}+\epsilon_{i}$ .

$$ \beta_{j}\mid\mathbf{r},\pi_{j},\tau^{2},\sigma^{2}\sim\begin{cases}\delta_{0}&\text{if }\pi_{j}=0\\[10.0pt] \mathcal{N}\left(\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}r_{i}x_{i}}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}^{2}+\frac{1}{\tau^{2}}},\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}^{2}+\frac{1}{\tau^{2}}}\right)&\text{if }\pi_{j}=1\end{cases} $$

- • Update Hyper-parameters If the problem is one dimensional, we have the following update rules, $\displaystyle\theta\mid\cdot=\theta\mid\pi\sim\text{ Beta }(A+\pi,B+1-\pi),$ $\displaystyle\tau^{2}\mid\beta,\mu,\pi=1\sim\text{ InvGamma }(b_{1}+\frac{1}{2},b_{2}+\frac{(\beta-\mu)^{2}}{2}),$ $\displaystyle\tau^{2}\mid\beta,\mu,\pi=0\sim\text{ InvGamma }(b_{1},b_{2}),$ $\displaystyle\mu\mid\beta,\tau^{2},\pi=1\sim\mathcal{N}\left(\frac{\frac{\mu_{0}}{\tau_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\beta}{\tau^{2}}}{\frac{1}{\tau_{0}^{2}}+\frac{1}{\tau^{2}}},\frac{1}{\frac{1}{\tau_{0}^{2}}+\frac{1}{\tau^{2}}}\right),$ $\displaystyle\mu\mid\beta,\tau^{2},\pi=0\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{0},\tau^{2}_{0}),$ $\displaystyle\sigma^{2}\mid y,\beta\sim\text{ InvGamma }(a_{1}+\frac{n}{2},a_{2}+\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_{i}-x_{i}\beta)^{2}}{2}).$ Now in general case, we have $\displaystyle\theta\mid\cdot=\theta\mid\pi\sim\text{ Beta }(A+\sum_{j}\pi_{j},B+\sum_{j}1-\pi_{j}),$ $\displaystyle\tau^{2}\mid\beta,\mu,\pi\sim\text{ InvGamma }(b_{1}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j}\pi_{j},b_{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j}\pi_{j}(\beta_{j}-\mu)^{2})\quad,$ $\displaystyle\mu\mid\beta,\tau^{2},\pi=1\sim\mathcal{N}\left(\frac{\frac{\mu_{0}}{\tau_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\sum_{j}\beta_{j}}{\tau^{2}}}{\frac{1}{\tau_{0}^{2}}+\frac{p}{\tau^{2}}},\frac{1}{\frac{1}{\tau_{0}^{2}}+\frac{p}{\tau^{2}}}\right),$ $\displaystyle\sigma^{2}\mid y,\beta\sim\text{ InvGamma }(a_{1}+\frac{n}{2},a_{2}+\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_{i}-x_{i}\beta)^{2}}{2}).$

### B.2 Spike-and-slab update rules for logistic model

Deriving scalable sampling methods for logistic model has been actively studied in the statistical literature Ray and Szabó (2022); Biswas et al. (2022); Barndorff-Nielsen et al. (1982); Biane et al. (2001); Polson et al. (2013). However, the sampling for Spike-and-Slab logistic model is much more trickier. The approach we use follows from the $t$ -distribution approximation for the logistic distribution in O’brien and Dunson (2004); Narisetty et al. (2019). We can approximate $\text{Logistic}(x_{i}^{T}\bm{\beta},1)$ with $x_{i}^{T}\bm{\beta}+wt_{\nu}$ , where $t_{\nu}$ denotes a t-distribution with $\nu$ degrees of freedom and $w$ is a multiplicative factor. The choice of the constants $\nu=7.3$ and $w^{2}=\frac{\pi^{2}(\nu-2)}{3\nu}$ were recommended by O’brien and Dunson (2004). This allows us to re-write the Spike-and-Slab logistic model as

$$ \displaystyle z_{j} \displaystyle\overset{iid}{\sim}\text{Bernoulli}(\theta_{j}), \displaystyle\beta_{j}\mid z_{j} \displaystyle\overset{ind}{\sim}(1-z_{j})\delta_{0}+z_{j}\mathcal{N}(\mu,\tau^{2}), \displaystyle\widetilde{\sigma}^{2} \displaystyle\overset{iid}{\sim}\text{InvGamma}(\frac{\nu}{2},\frac{w^{2}\nu}{2}), \displaystyle\widetilde{y}_{i}\mid\bm{\beta},\widetilde{\sigma}^{2} \displaystyle\overset{ind}{\sim}\mathcal{N}(x_{i}^{T}\bm{\beta},\widetilde{\sigma}^{2}), \displaystyle y_{i} \displaystyle=\mathbbm{1}(\widetilde{y}_{i}>0). $$

Thus it reduces to sample from the spike-and-slab linear model discussed in the previous sub-section.
